accounting.rationale: The list is nonempty and comma-separated through assumed R401. R401's definition is not duplicated as invented local original-source atoms.
The explicit object-name production R804/C810 overrides an assumed generic name rule; declaration role and attribute eligibility remain separate.

Normative statement-to-attribute mechanism for the listed objects. ALLOCATABLE meaning stays at 8.5.3 and actual allocation/status/lifetime operations at 9.7 and their other defining owners. No duplicate allocation-effect or no-op S requirement is invented.
8.5.1 permits either an attr-spec or an attribute specification statement. This is the R832 route; its occurrence is not an executable ALLOCATE operation.
PENDING a finite declaration/attribute-use relation to 8.5.3p1 and 8.2R802. The attribute does not itself allocate, define a payload, give unallocated bounds or establish pointer association.

Each actual listed object receives the attribute, subject to its canonical role and shape/coshape restrictions. A function result variable is distinct from a function-reference value, and a component declaration is not an arbitrary percent-designator in this statement.

8.5.3, 8.5.6/.8, 9.7, argument association and definedness keep their owners. Source/use or case-reuse relationships remain pending; no SourceUses instance, evidence link or incidental allocation credit is added.
The complete REAL A, B(:), SCALAR example and ALLOCATABLE declaration are on PDF135 before 8.6.3. It illustrates mixed declaration routes, not allocation or initialized data.
The example first supplies REAL type and B's array specification. This bounded order is not a blanket rule that all type/attribute specifications must always use this order.
A(:,:) supplies a rank-two deferred-shape array specification in the ALLOCATABLE statement, not bounds of an allocation or type-parameter arguments.
B's rank-one array specification is already present; bare B in the later statement still becomes allocatable. Repeating an array/attribute specification is not required.
SCALAR has no array specification or rank clause giving positive rank. It is a scalar allocatable, not an array of size zero; no allocation or value observation is supplied.

requirements.title: An ALLOCATABLE statement has an optional double colon and a nonempty declaration list
requirements.definition: The ALLOCATABLE keyword is followed by an optional double colon and an allocatable-decl list. The list contains at least one declaration and is comma-separated under R401. Each member uses R833; attribute eligibility, specification ordering and repeated-attribute restrictions retain their canonical owners.

pending.double-colon-form: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete ordinary main or module with prior INTEGER declaration and one ALLOCATABLE :: name statement. No initializer, POINTER, PARAMETER, COMMON or second explicit ALLOCATABLE specification; no allocation or data access is needed.
pending.no-double-colon-form: PENDING compile/positive-control: otherwise equivalent complete source uses ALLOCATABLE name. The optional separator is not made mandatory; source-form token separation must still be valid.
pending.multiple-distinct-objects: PENDING compile/positive-control: two or three separately typed distinct ordinary variables in one comma-separated ALLOCATABLE list, each receiving the attribute once. Do not use repeated aliases of the same entity to stand in for list syntax.
pending.mixed-declarator-list: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete the original note's REAL A, B(:), SCALAR and ALLOCATABLE :: A(:,:), B, SCALAR pattern. Preserve the prior and local array-spec routes and the true scalar. No unallocated payload, shape or bounds are read.
pending.missing-list-exclusion: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: a complete specification part contains ALLOCATABLE :: without an object list; repair only by inserting one prior-typed eligible scalar name. The source has no SAVE-like listless all-items form and no otherwise valid statement parse may be substituted.
pending.list-separator-repair: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: two prior-typed distinct eligible names are separated incorrectly, for example by a missing comma, with a one-comma repair. Keep declaration roles, shape and all other attributes valid; require the intended list-syntax origin, not a duplicate-attribute or unknown-name report.
pending.single-specification-source-gate: PENDING canonical 8.5.1/C815 and 8.2/R802 relationship: one explicit route is valid; a type-declaration ALLOCATABLE plus a second explicit statement is not a new R832 grammar violation. Existing C815 allocatable-statement diagnostic/control IDs, byte repairs, predicates and roles remain unchanged; no clone or numbered-target link is authored.
pending.scope-identity-source-gate: PENDING exact 5.3/11.1.4/14.2.2/19.4/19.5.1.4 source relations. An ALLOCATABLE statement can introduce a local identifier that hides a host name, and in BLOCK declares a construct entity. It is not permission to re-attribute an imported object. Any controls need complete local type declarations and actual object identity, not a value-printing proxy.

requirements.oracle: Complete compile admissions and single-predicate syntax/reporting contrasts with valid minimal repairs. The numbered grammar supplies reporting capability under 4.2p2(3), not mandatory fatal rejection, exact wording or printed R832. Source/use facets require an independently supported evidence mechanism before coverage.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No case is implemented here. Unknown names, wrong entity category, duplicate attribute, incompatible shape/coshape, unsupported facilities, source echoes, compiler crashes and resource failures cannot corroborate an isolated grammar negative. Declaration acceptance is not allocation, value retention or allocation-status evidence.

requirements.title: An allocatable declarator names an object with independently optional array and coarray specifications
requirements.definition: Each declarator is an object-name, optionally followed by a parenthesized array-spec and independently optionally followed by a bracketed coarray-spec, in that order. These are declaration specifications, not element references, type-parameter arguments or allocation bounds. Omitting a group does not discard a rank/corank specification validly supplied elsewhere. Canonical array, coarray and entity-role conditions still apply.

pending.scalar-name: PENDING compile/positive-control: a prior-typed ordinary INTEGER with no array-spec, positive RANK clause or coarray-spec is named in ALLOCATABLE. It is scalar; do not call it zero-sized, allocate it implicitly or inspect its value.
pending.deferred-array-spec: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete ordinary declarations use one- and two-colon forms name(:) and name(:,:) in the statement, with no earlier competing rank/array specification. The array rank is declared but the allocation, extents and bounds are not supplied by this syntax.
pending.scalar-coarray-spec: PENDING compile/positive-control: prior-typed scalar INTEGER is declared ALLOCATABLE as name[:], with no array parentheses. Retain C823/C824/C826 and C827's deferred-coshape requirement. This does not allocate the coarray or make cobounds/payload available.
pending.array-and-coarray-spec: PENDING compile/positive-control: ordinary INTEGER name(:,:)[:] uses both optional groups, array first. Choose small rank/corank satisfying C822 and valid allocatable coarray roles. No runtime image, synchronization, allocation or descriptor oracle is inferred.
pending.prior-array-spec: PENDING compile/positive-control: REAL B(:) precedes ALLOCATABLE :: B, as in the original note; a separate legal DIMENSION route is a canonical alternative. Do not require the suffix to be repeated or declare this ultimately allocatable array invalid merely because the earlier line has no ALLOCATABLE spelling.
pending.prior-coarray-spec: PENDING compile/positive-control: a scalar INTEGER has a prior deferred CODIMENSION specification, followed by ALLOCATABLE naming it without a second coarray-spec. The final declaration satisfies C827; retain R837/R838 ownership and no duplicate explicit CODIMENSION specification.
pending.rank-clause-source-relation: PENDING original RANK-clause/C834 declaration relationship: an eligible small constant RANK can supply rank while this statement supplies ALLOCATABLE. Do not add a conflicting second array specification or copy the separately frozen RANK source packet. Rank-clause eligibility and actual rank observations keep their own owners.
pending.whole-name-not-designator: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: complete type definition and ordinary TYPE(record) object precede ALLOCATABLE :: object%member. Repair by deleting %member so the whole eligible object is named. R833 has object-name, not a data-ref or structure-component alternative; declarations of allocatable components remain owned by 7.5.4.
pending.declarator-delimiters-and-order: PENDING separate complete syntax contrasts for one missing array parenthesis, one missing coarray bracket, and reversed coarray/array groups. Repair only the selected delimiter or group order and retain eligible deferred shape/coshape, object type and statement context. Do not combine independent malformed sites in one diagnostic claim.
pending.type-parameter-separation: PENDING compile/source controls with an already typed CHARACTER(len=3) scalar and a CHARACTER(len=3) array: length is established by the type declaration, while any parentheses here supply array specification. A deferred CHARACTER length or PDT parameter route needs its own C702/type-parameter premises and must not repeat an already explicit ALLOCATABLE attribute.
pending.declaration-role-source-gate: PENDING complete ordinary, dummy and separately named function-result-variable contexts, preserving required explicit interfaces. Include a genuine allocatable assumed-rank dummy declared with name(..), no CODIMENSION/VALUE and only C840-permitted uses; it is not an ordinary deferred-shape array or an ordinary local. A called allocatable result must be properly defined under 15.6.2.2; its returned value is not the declared object. Other entity categories need their exact canonical role/diagnostic basis, not automatic R833 rejection credit.
pending.shape-and-coshape-owner-gates: PENDING C834/C827 source relations: generic array-spec/coarray-spec grammar does not make explicit bounds or explicit coshape legal for an allocatable array/coarray. Existing C834 contrasts retain their owners and roles. Assumed-rank dummy use has C839/C840 premises; no ordinary assumed-shape or assumed-size allocatable control is manufactured, and no numbered-target reuse is forced.

requirements.oracle: Complete declared-object syntax controls, with independent rank/corank/role conditions and source-minimal grammatical repairs. R804/C810 govern object-name; C834 and C827 govern the constrained shape/coshape choices. Source relations are pending rather than duplicate programs or evidence links.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The ALLOCATABLE statement is not ALLOCATE and has no SOURCE=/MOLD=/STAT= allocation interface. Type parameters do not become rank/corank and an array specification is not a selected element. Deferred shape/coshape is not a deferred type parameter; a nonconstant nondeferred length can still meet 8.3's automatic-object definition. No unallocated data/bounds/cobounds/deferred-parameter inquiry, blanket initially-unallocated dummy claim, heap/stack/address or process-status oracle is allowed.
